chunk.text: This club was once mocked, even by me a few weeks ago. Across European football, people were saying the club was finished, that there was no life left in it. But today, if I say Manchester United is one of the most dangerous football teams right now, I wouldn’t be wrong. Bruno Fernandes is there—the best number 10 in the world at the moment. He has single-handedly revived that role. The passes he played yesterday were unbelievable. Even legends didn’t always play with this level of creativity. He was delivering incredible diagonal balls.

The way he was feeding players like Mbeumo and Cunha was elite. He is in incredible form. The kind of passes he is making—it’s not something you expect from a young midfielder. The confidence level is unreal. Michael Carrick stays calm, doesn’t talk much, and focuses on simple, logical football. And the players are delivering. Tottenham tried to play a mid-block, trying to stay compact and cautious, but United broke them down piece by piece. It was football excellence. The movement of Mbeumo and Cunha was outstanding.

Look at the difference in setups. Under the previous system, players were out of position. But now it’s simple—common sense football. Players are playing in their natural roles. However, one interesting thing is that United are not starting with a traditional number 9. Players like Zirkzee and others are on the bench, while Mbeumo, Cunha, and Bruno are leading the attack fluidly.

The numbers are insane. The number of passes, the control in midfield—everything is at a high level. Bruno Fernandes is among the fastest players to reach 200 goal contributions. Everyone knows the form he is in. Honestly, if this United team faces Real Madrid right now, they could dominate. That’s the level they are playing at.

This is not a joke. Watching the game, I was surprised. With such limited training time under Carrick, how are they playing like this? It shows that sometimes it’s just about common sense. And honestly, common sense is rare in football today.

To bring out the best in players, you need to understand them at a human level. That’s what Carrick seems to be doing. The intensity, the running, the pressing—it’s all at another level. Compared to previous systems, this feels more natural and committed.

United’s philosophy is clear—high pressing, quick ball recovery, and strong intensity. They don’t rely on long balls unnecessarily. Instead, they keep things simple and effective. In the last six games, they have the most final-third ball recoveries in the league.

Player selection is key. They are choosing players who genuinely press and fight for the ball. Mbeumo and Cunha have been fantastic signings. The defensive line gives no breathing space. It’s a nightmare for opponents.
What stands out is the clarity of thought and trust in the manager. The pressing system is well-organized. Players understand their roles perfectly, maintaining structure and compactness.

This team is extremely well connected. The players are close to each other on the pitch, both physically and tactically. It shows great understanding. This level of coordination is what defines a strong team.

Michael Carrick has the potential to become a top coach. He has learned from great managers like Sir Alex Ferguson and José Mourinho. However, one key point—players like Lisandro Martínez are crucial. Without him, the system struggles.

Lisandro Martínez brings confidence and composure. Pressing him is difficult because he reads the game so well. Then you have Kobbie Mainoo, one of the best young midfielders right now. His composure and awareness are exceptional.
Mainoo provides incredible control in midfield. No matter the situation, he stays calm and delivers. His impact is massive. Whenever he starts, United performs at a very high level.
Casemiro is also benefiting from this system. The team supports him with short passing options, reducing pressure on him. This allows him to focus on his strengths—simple and effective play.
Every player is being used correctly. It’s basic football, but executed perfectly. Confidence is the key. Right now, it’s hard to find weaknesses in this team.
Another dangerous team right now is Barcelona. Lamine Yamal, before turning 19, is already breaking records. He is currently the best winger in the world. There is no doubt about it.
What he does on the ball is magical. His impact is similar to how Messi influenced teams in his early years. Coaches rely on top players like him, and that’s completely normal.
Yamal is not just good on the ball but also off it. He has the highest pressing and ball recoveries among wingers in La Liga. That shows discipline and hunger.

Football changes quickly. A few weeks ago, things were different. Now everything has changed. That’s the beauty of the game—anything can happen at any moment. Let’s see what happens next. See you in the next video.
